title_en: Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Property Rights Part of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 Where a dispute arises over the ownership of a real property right, or over the sale, gift, mortgage, etc. that serves as the basis for the registration of a real property right, and a party initiates a civil action, the action shall be accepted according to law, except where the party has already applied in an administrative action for a joint resolution of the aforesaid civil dispute and the People's Court hears it jointly.

Article 2 Where a party has evidence proving that the entry in the real estate register is inconsistent with the true state of rights and that such party is the true holder of the real property right, and petitions for the confirmation of its real right, the petition shall be upheld.

Article 3 After a caveat registration becomes invalid due to the circumstances specified in the second paragraph of Article 220 of the Civil Code, if a party initiates a civil action petitioning for the confirmation of the ownership of a real right, the action shall be accepted according to law. The invalidity of the caveat registration shall not affect the substantive trial of the case by the People's Court.

Article 4 Where, without the consent of the holder of a priority notice registration, the ownership of a real property or other real rights are transferred, or other real rights such as construction land use right, habitation right, easement, or mortgage right are created, the act shall be determined to have no real right effect in accordance with the provisions of the first paragraph of Article 221 of the Civil Code.

Article 5 Where an agreement for the sale of a real property right that has been registered under a priority notice is determined to be void, or is revoked, or the holder of the priority notice registration relinquishes its claim, it shall be determined that the “obligation or claim is extinguished” as referred to in the second paragraph of Article 221 of the Civil Code.

Article 6 Where a transferor transfers the ownership of a vessel, aircraft, motor vehicle, or the like, and the transferee has paid a reasonable price and taken possession thereof, if, despite the lack of registration, a creditor of the transferor claims that it is a “bona fide third party” as referred to in Article 225 of the Civil Code, such claim shall not be upheld, unless otherwise provided by law.

Article 7 A judgment, award, or consent judgment rendered and taking legal effect according to law in a case involving the partition of co-owned immovable or movable property, or the like, by a People's Court or an arbitration institution, which alters the original real right relationship, as well as a ruling for a successful auction, a ruling for a successful sale, or a ruling for transfer of property in satisfaction of a debt made by a People's Court during enforcement proceedings, shall be determined as the legal instrument of the People's Court or the arbitration institution that causes the creation, alteration, transfer, or extinguishment of a real right as referred to in Article 229 of the Civil Code.

Article 8 Where a holder of a real right, who enjoys the real right pursuant to Articles 229 to 231 of the Civil Code but has not yet completed the delivery of the movable property or the registration of the immovable property, petitions for the protection of its real right in accordance with Articles 235 to 238 of the Civil Code, the petition shall be upheld.

Article 9 When the holder of a right to a co-owned share changes due to inheritance, legacy, or other reasons, if other co-owners by shares claim a right of first refusal, such claim shall not be upheld, unless otherwise agreed among the co-owners by shares.

Article 10 The “equivalent conditions” as referred to in Article 305 of the Civil Code shall be determined by comprehensively considering factors such as the transfer price of the co-owned share, the method and term for payment of the price, and other relevant factors.

Article 11 The period for exercising the right of first refusal shall be governed by the agreement among the co-owners by shares if there is one; in the absence of an agreement or if the agreement is unclear, it shall be determined in accordance with the following circumstances: (1) If the period for exercise is specified in the notice containing the contents of the equivalent conditions sent by the transferor to the other co-owners by shares, such period shall prevail; (2) If the notice does not specify the period for exercise, or if the specified period is shorter than fifteen days from the date of service of the notice, the period shall be fifteen days; (3) If the transferor fails to give notice, the period shall be fifteen days from the date on which the other co-owners by shares know or should have known the final equivalent conditions; (4) If the transferor fails to give notice and it is impossible to determine when the other co-owners by shares knew or should have known the final equivalent conditions, the period shall be six months from the date of transfer of the right to the co-owned share.

Article 12 Where a co-owner by shares transfers its share to a person other than the co-owners, and another co-owner by shares petitions to purchase the co-owned share by right of first refusal under equivalent conditions in accordance with the provisions of laws and judicial interpretations, the petition shall be upheld. The petition of another co-owner by shares shall not be upheld in any of the following circumstances: (1) The right of first refusal is not claimed within the period specified in Article 11 of this Interpretation, or although the right of first refusal is claimed, a substantive modification such as a reduction in the transfer price or an increase in the transferor's burden is proposed; (2) Only the revocation of the contract for the transfer of the co-owned share or the invalidity of such contract is claimed on the ground that the right of first refusal has been infringed.

Article 13 Where a co-owner by shares transfers a co-owned share to another co-owner by shares, and other co-owners by shares claim the right of first refusal in accordance with Article 305 of the Civil Code, such claim shall not be upheld, unless otherwise agreed among the co-owners by shares.

Article 14 Where, at the time of acquiring immovable or movable property, the transferee did not know that the transferor had no right of disposition and was not grossly negligent, the transferee shall be determined to have acted in good faith. If the true holder of the right claims that the transferee did not act in good faith, the true holder shall bear the burden of adducing evidence and the burden of proof.

Article 15 In any of the following circumstances, the transferee of the immovable property shall be determined to have known that the transferor had no right of disposition: (1) There is a valid caveat registration on the register; (2) During the effective period of a priority notice registration, the transaction is conducted without the consent of the holder of the priority notice registration; (3) Matters concerning the sealing up, freezing, or other forms of restriction on the right to the immovable property by a judicial or administrative organ according to law are already recorded on the register; (4) The transferee knows that the holder of the right recorded on the register is incorrect; (5) The transferee knows that another person already enjoys the real right in the immovable property according to law. If the true holder has evidence proving that the transferee of the immovable property should have known that the transferor had no right of disposition, the transferee shall be determined to have been grossly negligent.

Article 16 Where, at the time the transferee acquires the movable property, the subject, place, or timing of the transaction does not conform to trading practices, the transferee shall be determined to have been grossly negligent.

Article 17 The phrase “at the time the transferee acquires the immovable or movable property” as referred to in subparagraph (1) of the first paragraph of Article 311 of the Civil Code means the time when the transfer of the real property right is registered or when the movable property is delivered according to law. If the parties deliver the movable property in the manner prescribed in Article 226 of the Civil Code, the time of delivery of the movable property shall be the time when the civil legal act for the transfer of the movable property takes effect; if the parties deliver the movable property in the manner prescribed in Article 227 of the Civil Code, the time of delivery of the movable property shall be the time when the agreement between the transferor and the transferee on the transfer of the right to claim the return of the original property takes effect. If there are other provisions of law on the creation of real rights in immovable or movable property, the time for determining whether the holder is in good faith shall be in accordance with the time prescribed by law.

Article 18 The “reasonable price” as referred to in subparagraph (2) of the first paragraph of Article 311 of the Civil Code shall be comprehensively determined in accordance with the specific circumstances such as the nature and quantity of the subject matter of the transfer and the method of payment, with reference to factors such as the market price at the place of transaction at the time of transfer and trading practices.

Article 19 Where the transferor delivers vessels, aircraft, motor vehicles, or the like as specified in Article 225 of the Civil Code to the transferee, it shall be determined that the conditions for bona fide acquisition as stipulated in subparagraph (3) of the first paragraph of Article 311 of the Civil Code are satisfied.

Article 20 In any of the following circumstances, if the transferee claims to have acquired ownership in accordance with Article 311 of the Civil Code, such claim shall not be upheld: (1) The contract of transfer is determined to be void; (2) The contract of transfer is revoked.
Article 21 This Interpretation shall come into force as of January 1, 2021.
